departments.name: Quality Assurance
departments.mission: Prove the game works and refuse anything that does not: gameplay, collision, AI, UI, saves, multiplayer and build verification.
capabilities: collision, AI, UI and save/load testing

deliverables.name: Test Plan
acceptance: Every system in the GDD mapped to at least one test case
Automated versus manual split stated with commands to run
Entry and exit criteria defined per test cycle
Device and platform coverage matches the compatibility matrix

deliverables.name: Test Report
acceptance: Pass and fail counts with the exact commands and builds tested
Every failure linked to a bug report with reproduction steps
Blocking defects called out separately from cosmetic ones

deliverables.name: Regression Suite and Sign-off
acceptance: Regression suite runs green on the release candidate
No open blocker or critical bug at sign-off
Every skipped test listed with the reason it was skipped

gates: An untested claim of 'works' in a deliverable is rejected
A skipped check without a recorded reason is rejected

departments.name: Performance Engineering
departments.mission: Hold the frame budget on real hardware: CPU, GPU, memory, draw calls, LOD, streaming, shaders and mobile scaling.

deliverables.name: Performance Budget
acceptance: A budget per hardware class using the studio performance profiles
Frame, CPU, GPU, memory and draw-call ceilings stated in numbers
Quality tiers defined with what changes between them
Measurement method and tooling named

deliverables.name: Profiling Report
acceptance: Measured average and 1%-low FPS on every declared platform and device
Top hotspots ranked with measured cost, not guesses
Memory and draw calls measured against the budget
Every over-budget item has an owner and a fix

deliverables.name: Optimisation Pass
acceptance: Re-measured results after fixes, on the same devices and method
Frame pacing verified: no recurring spike pattern
Lowest quality tier playable on the weakest declared device
Remaining misses listed honestly with impact

inputs: scene costs from D08, D12, D13
gates: A performance claim without device, method and numbers is rejected
A release candidate failing its frame target on a declared platform is blocked

departments.name: Compatibility Engineering
departments.mission: Make the game run correctly everywhere it ships: platforms, hardware classes, resolutions, controllers, touch and input parity.
capabilities: hardware class matrices (low, mid, high, tablet, desktop)

deliverables.name: Device and Platform Matrix
acceptance: Every target platform and hardware class listed with a representative device
Minimum specification stated per platform
Input devices and required parity listed
Which classes are supported versus best-effort is explicit

deliverables.name: Compatibility Test Matrix
acceptance: Every row tested on the named device or emulator with a result
Resolution, orientation and safe-area behaviour verified
Failures converted to bug reports with device details

deliverables.name: Input Parity Review
acceptance: Every action reachable with every declared input device
Touch targets and gestures verified on a real mobile viewport
Remapping and accessibility inputs verified

gates: An untested platform claimed as supported is rejected
An action unreachable on a declared input device is a release blocker

departments.name: Security and Reliability
departments.mission: Keep saves, sessions and servers trustworthy: validation, anti-cheat structure, crash recovery, error handling and dependency risk.

deliverables.name: Threat Model
acceptance: Assets, actors and trust boundaries enumerated
Each threat rated with impact and likelihood
Every client-supplied value listed with its server validation rule
Secrets handling and storage stated

deliverables.name: Security Hardening
acceptance: Save tampering and malformed input rejected without crashing
Abuse paths tested and rate limited
Dependency audit run with findings triaged

deliverables.name: Release Integrity Audit
acceptance: No critical or high unmitigated finding remains
Credentials absent from client code, logs and shipped files
Rollback or recovery procedure documented and tested once

gates: A client-authoritative economy or progression value is a release blocker
Any secret found in shipped files blocks release

departments.name: Asset Acquisition
departments.mission: Find and clear assets the studio may legally ship: search the libraries, verify licences and record provenance for everything.
capabilities: searching 3D model, texture, animation and audio libraries

deliverables.name: Asset Plan
acceptance: Every needed asset class listed as sourced, original or to-be-decided
Licence requirement stated per class (commercial use mandatory)
Reuse candidates named from the existing studio libraries
Budget and timeline per asset class stated

deliverables.name: Sourced Asset Records
acceptance: Every sourced asset has id, creator, source URL, licence and hash
No asset is marked usable without a verified commercial licence
Format and scale compatibility verified by an import test
Attribution list generated for every CC BY asset

deliverables.name: Licence Audit
acceptance: Every shipped asset traced to a record in the catalogue
Zero unverified, non-commercial or share-alike assets in the build
Attribution file included where licences require it

gates: An asset with unknown or non-commercial licence blocks release
A CC BY asset without recorded attribution is rejected

departments.name: Asset Integration
departments.mission: Get assets into the build correctly: import, convert, optimise, name, wire collisions and keep the reusable library healthy.
capabilities: geometry and texture optimisation on import

deliverables.name: Asset Pipeline Conventions
acceptance: Naming pattern defined for meshes, materials, textures and animations
Folder layout and import settings stated
Provenance and licence metadata carried with each imported asset
Import validation rules (scale, pivot, units) listed

deliverables.name: Asset Integration Pass
acceptance: Every required asset imported, named to convention and referenced in code
Imported assets respect triangle, texture and memory budgets
Licence metadata present for every imported asset
No missing, pink or fallback-material assets in the build

deliverables.name: Integration Review
acceptance: Build loads every asset with zero 404 or decode errors
Instancing and reuse opportunities taken where they exist
Asset load time measured against the stated budget

gates: Fallback or untextured assets in a build are rejected
An imported asset without provenance is rejected

departments.name: Technical Art
departments.mission: Bridge art and engineering: shaders, material systems, procedural tools, rendering pipelines and art production tooling.

deliverables.name: Shader and Pipeline Plan
acceptance: Every custom shader listed with purpose, variants and fallback
Material parameter contract shared with D09
Shader cost ceiling stated per quality tier
Mobile shader constraints stated explicitly

deliverables.name: Shaders and Art Tools
acceptance: Every listed shader implemented with a working fallback
Tools run reproducibly from documented commands
Shader variants counted against the stated ceiling

deliverables.name: Pipeline Review
acceptance: Measured shader and pipeline cost per quality tier
Variant explosion or unused variants reported and pruned
Tooling failures surfaced instead of silently producing bad assets

gates: A shader without a fallback for the lowest tier is rejected
A tool that fails silently is rejected

departments.name: Production Management
departments.mission: Ship it: scheduling, milestones, dependencies, builds, documentation and the release checklist nobody is allowed to skip.

deliverables.name: Production Plan
acceptance: Milestones with dates, owners and exit criteria
Dependency graph of deliverables and the critical path
Scope, budget and risk register with mitigations
Definition of done agreed with the Studio Director

deliverables.name: Milestone Report
acceptance: Every milestone marked met or missed with evidence
Blocked and at-risk items listed with owners
Scope changes recorded with their approvals

deliverables.name: Release Checklist and Build Record
acceptance: Every gate signed off with a link to its evidence
Built artefact identified by version, commit and build command
Install and launch verified from the shipped artefact on a declared platform
Known issues shipped with the build, not hidden

gates: A release without a passing QA, performance and licence gate is blocked
A shipped known-issue list that hides a blocker is rejected
